author: blu
body: Authentication answers Maybe, and the reason is that the alternative was unsound rather than merely untidy. This used to return an ExternalIdentity from both arms: an unreadable id token produced a record with an empty subject and the provider's REAL access and refresh tokens, which bridge-add-identity then stored and bridge-get-access-token then handed out. Nothing downstream could tell that identity from an authenticated one, and bridge-provider-score vouches for its provider at 6000 either way. A token the bridge could not read is not a user, so there is no identity to return.
